Black_Rust.name: Wheat - Black Rust (Stem Rust)
Black_Rust.cause: Fungus: Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici
Black_Rust.symptoms: Dark brown to black raised pustules on stems and leaf sheaths, reddish-brown spores released when pustules rupture. Leaves may yellow and wither.
Black_Rust.treatment: Plant resistant varieties. Apply triazole-based fungicides (propiconazole, tebuconazole) at first sign. Remove volunteer wheat and alternate grass hosts. Avoid late sowing.

Flag_Smut.name: Wheat - Flag Smut
Flag_Smut.symptoms: Long, dark, longitudinal streaks on leaves (especially the flag leaf), leaf sheaths, and stems. Affected leaves may curl and shred. Severely infected plants are stunted.
Flag_Smut.treatment: Use smut-free certified seed. Treat seed with carboxin or thiram-based fungicide. Remove and destroy infected plants. Rotate away from wheat for 2-3 years.

Foot_Rot.name: Wheat - Foot Rot (Crown Rot)
Foot_Rot.symptoms: Browning and necrosis of the stem base (crown), whiteheads appearing prematurely, reduced tillering, and lodge-prone stems.
Foot_Rot.treatment: Rotate with non-cereals for at least 2 years. Avoid excess irrigation. Apply seed fungicide (tebuconazole + fludioxonil). Remove crop residues.

Hill_Bunt_Common_Bunt.name: Wheat - Hill Bunt / Common Bunt (Loose Smut complex)
Hill_Bunt_Common_Bunt.cause: Fungus: Tilletia caries (Common Bunt) / Tilletia laevis (Stinking Smut)
Hill_Bunt_Common_Bunt.symptoms: Bunt balls replacing grain kernels inside the spike, emitting a strong fishy odor when broken open. Ears may appear silvery-grey before rupture.
Hill_Bunt_Common_Bunt.treatment: Use certified bunt-free seed. Treat seed with carboxin-thiram or difenoconazole. Sow resistant varieties. Deep plowing to bury infected debris.

Leaf_Blight.name: Wheat - Leaf Blight
Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Small, oval, light-brown to dark lesions on leaves with concentric rings. Lesions coalesce causing large necrotic patches and premature leaf drying.
Leaf_Blight.treatment: Apply foliar fungicide (mancozeb or propiconazole) at early symptom appearance. Ensure balanced nitrogen fertilization. Avoid overhead irrigation. Use resistant varieties.

Leaf_Rust.name: Wheat - Leaf Rust (Brown Rust)
Leaf_Rust.symptoms: Small, round to oval, orange-brown pustules scattered on upper leaf surfaces. Leaves yellow and dry from tip downward in severe infection.
Leaf_Rust.treatment: Plant resistant/tolerant varieties. Apply triazole or strobilurin fungicides when disease threshold is reached. Avoid early sowing in high-risk zones.

Loose_Smut.name: Wheat - Loose Smut
Loose_Smut.symptoms: Entire ear replaced by a mass of black, powdery spores enclosed in a thin membrane that ruptures at flowering. Stalks may be affected. No grain produced in infected ears.
Loose_Smut.treatment: Use systemic seed treatments (carboxin-thiram or tebuconazole). Sow resistant varieties. Remove infected heads before spores disperse.

Powdery_Mildew.name: Wheat - Powdery Mildew
Powdery_Mildew.cause: Fungus: Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici
Powdery_Mildew.symptoms: White to grey powdery patches on upper leaf surfaces, stems, and leaf sheaths. Heavily infected leaves turn yellow and may die.
Powdery_Mildew.treatment: Apply triazole-based fungicides (propiconazole, tebuconazole) at first sign. Plant resistant varieties. Avoid dense planting and excessive nitrogen.

Wheat_Blast.name: Wheat - Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae pathotype Triticum)
Wheat_Blast.symptoms: Bleached lesions at the spike base, causing partial or complete sterility of the spike (blank ears). Leaf lesions are diamond-shaped with grey centers.
Wheat_Blast.treatment: No fully effective chemical control exists. Plant blast-resistant varieties. Avoid excessive nitrogen and late planting. Ensure adequate field drainage. Use tricyclazole as a preventive measure.

Yellow_Rust.name: Wheat - Yellow Rust (Stripe Rust)
Yellow_Rust.cause: Fungus: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici
Yellow_Rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in long stripes along leaf veins. Severe infection causes leaves to dry up. Favored by cool, humid conditions.
Yellow_Rust.treatment: Use resistant varieties suited to your region. Apply fungicides (propiconazole, tebuconazole) at early stripe appearance. Remove alternate hosts. Avoid late sowing in rust-prone areas.

Wheat_Healthy.name: Wheat - Healthy
Wheat_Healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms. Leaves are uniformly green with normal growth and grain filling.
Wheat_Healthy.treatment: Continue regular scouting. Maintain balanced fertilization, proper irrigation schedule, and crop rotation to prevent future disease outbreaks.
